title: Entropy-driven microbucket KV placement and soft-reshard playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem statement: As batch sizes and concurrency grow under continuous batching, the KV cache exhibits long-tail fragmentation driven by skewed token fingerprints and transient hot keys. Existing slab-based strategies lead to uneven bucket utilization, frequent small-object churn, and periodic full compactions that spike GPU memory traffic. Goal: introduce a placement+reshard strategy that (1) reduces fragmentation by grouping KV entries by fingerprint entropy and affinity, (2) supports low-cost background soft-reshards (incremental migration) to rebalance hot/cold microbuckets without blocking inference, and (3) integrates with the batching/runtime scheduler to minimize cross-GPU fetches and prefetch misses.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end prototype deployed to canary fleet without impacting 99th percentile P99 latency by >5%
Measured reduction in percentiles of free-fragmentation (measured as total free segments / total allocated segments) by >=35% on 3 representative workloads
Decrease in background compaction I/O (GPU->CPU transfers) by >=40% during steady-state compared to current compact-on-threshold strategy
No increased tail error rate or memory OOM events in canary for 72h
Telemetry dashboards: per-bucket occupancy, migration-rate, slot-locality, and cross-GPU fetch ratio added to Console
technical_notes: Overview of approach: 1) Microbucketization: partition the KV index space into many small, fixed-size 'microbuckets' (e.g., 128-512 slots) assigned per-GPU memory region. 2) Entropy fingerprinting: compute a low-cost token-fingerprint entropy score (e.g., rolling 64-bit XOR+population-count) per KV key to separate highly-variant vs repetitive key patterns. 3) Affinity tagging: each request in the batch is annotated with batch-local affinity tag (recently accessed neighbors) so co-accessed KV entries are preferentially packed into the same microbucket. 4) Soft-reshard background mover: a rate-limited migrator performs shadow-copy of microbucket slots to a target GPU/region when occupancy diverges from watermarks. Migration is staged with three phases: snapshot, validate, and atomic pointer-swap; reads continue against the snapshot during migration to avoid stall. 5) Staggered eviction hysteresis: eviction thresholds are bucket-local and use decay-based hysteresis to avoid repeated churning. 6) Micro-slab packing: small entries are coalesced into fixed micro-slab pages to reduce per-entry overhead and alignment waste. 7) Integration with continuous batching: the scheduler exposes expected batch affinity maps to the allocator so microbuckets are placed to minimize cross-device fetches and maximize KV hot-path cache hits.
design_tradeoffs: More microbuckets increases placement granularity and reduces internal fragmentation but increases metadata overhead (per-bucket watermarks + migration state)
Entropy-based grouping risks misclassification for short-lived keys; mitigated via short TTL and immediate re-evaluation after repeated accesses
Soft-reshard background migration reduces tail spikes vs synchronous compaction but requires careful rate-limiting to not saturate PCIe or GPU copy engines
Packing small entries into micro-slabs increases serialization/deserialization cost slightly, but significantly reduces wasted alignment space for small tokens
implementation_plan: Phase 0 - Prototype (2 wks): implement lightweight fingerprinting and microbucket metadata in local dev runtime; add counters for occupancy and free-fragments
Phase 1 - Canary (3 wks): implement soft-reshard migrator with rate limiter; deploy to 5% canary; integrate scheduler hints for batch affinity; observe latency and migration IO

Phase 2 - Metrics & Safety (2 wks): add dashboards (per-bucket occupancy, migration latency, cross-GPU fetch ratio), slow-path fallback to current compacting allocator when migration backlog > threshold
Phase 3 - Gradual rollout (4 wks): increase traffic to 25% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback gates; tune bucket sizes and migration rates per workload profile
Phase 4 - Optimization (ongoing): micro-slab allocation tweaks, per-model quantization-aware packing, and heuristics for long-tail cold retention
rollout_plan: Canary fleet: select two clusters (chat-optimized short-seq workload + embedding bulk-lookup workload). Start with off-peak windows. Automatic rollback if P99 latency regresses >5% for two consecutive 1h windows or if OOMs observed. Manual safety gates for migration IO > configured threshold.
telemetry_metrics: cross_gpu_fetch_ratio (fraction of KV accesses that hit remote device)
backwards_compatibility: Allocator exposes config flags and a runtime feature-flag. If enabled, allocation decisions route to microbucket allocator; if disabled, existing slab allocator preserved. Migration component can be disabled via runtime flag for safe rollback.
open_risks: PCIe/GPU DMA saturation during large-scale migrations — mitigated with token bucket rate limiter and migration scheduling windows
Metadata blowup on extreme scale (millions of microbuckets) — mitigate by sharding metadata and aggregating low-activity buckets into meta-buckets
Wrong entropy classification causing hot keys to be trapped in cold buckets — mitigate with rapid hot promotion via access counters and immediate microbucket reselection
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprinting, bucket assignment, and atomic pointer-swap. Integration tests for migration correctness under concurrent reads/writes (fuzz with randomized access patterns). Load tests with synthetic skews (zipfian, bursty) and long-run soak tests to validate fragmentation metrics. Chaos tests that kill the migrator mid-migration to validate recovery semantics.
